earlier_scan.note: Glottolog: unattested; Kuikuru report speakers used Yawalapiti; no linguistic documentation exists at all.

sources.citation: Mujica, Mitzila Isabel Ortega. 1992. Aspectos fonológicos e gramaticais da língua Yawalapiti (Aruak). MA thesis, Unicamp (IEL). PDF via Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú (etnolinguistica.org/tese:mujica-1992)
sources.note: If the catalog wants a stress value for the speech the Agavotoqueng reportedly used, this is the deciding Yawalapiti (yawa1261) description; already held and quoted in the catalog under yawa1261 (lexical: final vs penult, minimal pairs). Not a description of agav1236.

sources.note: Nothing. 'a supposed, extinct Arawakan language of Brazil'; Glottolog 'unattested, which suggests that any classification is ethnic rather than linguistic'; no wordlist or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page 'Unattested: Agavotaguerra' (agav1236), Hammarström et al.,https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/agav1236
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States: 'Agavotaguerra is not attested, and the only information available are reports by the Kuikuru, who say the Agavotaguerra speak the same language as the Yawalapiti [yaw] (Galvão & Simões 1965: 23, Villas Boas 1975, Villas Boas & Villas Boas 1972: 45).' AES status extinct. Zero descriptive references.
